answer: Same-challenge clone collision test. Each epoch a public terrace posts one random challenge. Every identity must return a signed response from its hardware root and monotonic counter. Clones cannot diverge, so copies of one root produce identical responses; duplicate responses are rejected. To pass, an attacker must provision a distinct hardware root, apply a velvet tamper seal, and run a 2^20-step memory-hard setup per identity. A nebula feed supplies fresh randomness so responses cannot be precomputed. Extra identities therefore cost one physical key and roughly ten minutes of setup each.
